page: Microsoft Azure D4ns_v6 is a general purpose virtual machine instance running on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is provisioned with 4 vCPUs derived from 2 dedicated physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture incorporates 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 260 MB of L3 cache per physical package, alongside instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel AMX. Memory capacity is configured at 16.0 GB RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. No local storage is bundled, requiring the use of remote storage volumes, and the configuration contains no hardware GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier single-threaded capability coupled with restrained multi-core scale. The single-core stress-ng score reaches 1695.38 and PassMark CPU reaches 7079.45, both placing in the median performance bracket. Cryptographic and compression tests also align with average throughput tiers, supported by hardware AES-NI and SHA extensions. However, multi-core metrics, such as the multi-threaded stress-ng score of 3448.02 and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 23.02 GB/s, measure in the lower 25 percent bracket due to the physical two-core ceiling.

Memory bandwidth benchmarks register 32.41 GB/s for uncached large-block reads and 23.58 GB/s for writes, which fall into lower tiers relative to larger instances. In application workloads, the machine delivers 7.42 GB/s in static web serving and 5.29 million operations per second in Redis SET tests. Inference with a small 135M parameter language model achieves 580.96 prompt tokens per second, but drops to 29.96 tokens per second when evaluating medium 7B models.

The qualitative trade-off of the D4ns_v6 rests on its balanced general-purpose allocation without onboard local disk overhead. It is well suited for web serving, microservices, continuous integration tasks, and intermediate application hosting where moderate compute density is sufficient and persistent state is offloaded to managed network storage.
description: Microsoft Azure D4ns_v6 is a general purpose virtual machine configured with 4 vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM, backed by a dedicated 2-core Intel Xeon 8573C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz. Based on x86_64 architecture with AVX-512 and AMX extensions, it delivers balanced per-core resources with 4.0 GB of memory per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage or hardware accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage. Benchmark evaluations show solid median single-core CPU execution, PassMark metrics, and static web throughput of 7.42 GB/s, while multi-core workloads and memory bandwidth remain constrained by the underlying two-core hyperthreaded layout. The server profile is suited for standard web application hosting, containerized microservices, light batch processing, and non-intensive background jobs requiring balanced compute and memory capacity.
